summary.headline: M&M Financial Q4 FY26 PAT rose 55% YoY to INR 873 crore, but included a INR 217 crore macro overlay; FY26 PAT up 19% to INR 2,782 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 profit was driven by NIM expansion of 101 bps YoY and fee income growth, with credit cost held at 1.5% including a INR 217 crore management overlay (0.9% without it). Without the overlay, Q4 PAT would have been above INR 1,000 crore (84% growth). GS3 fell to 3.4% (down 39 bps QoQ) and GS2+GS3 hit 8.18%, both described as record lows. Management said growth regained momentum from H2 FY26, with AUM growth at 12%, and guided to a 16-18% medium-term CAGR.

financial_highlights.change: +60 bps FY YoY; +101 bps Q4 YoY

financial_highlights.value: 1.5% (0.9% ex-overlay; INR 560 crore incl. overlay, INR 343 crore ex-overlay)

financial_highlights.change: vs about 53% at Q3; about 53-55% ex-overlay

financial_highlights.metric: Fee and other income to assets

financial_highlights.change: from 6.3%; one-offs from rights issue cited

segments.name: Wheels / tractors
segments.commentary: Tractor disbursements grew 63% in FY26 (overall disbursements +49%); passenger vehicle AUM grew 14% with Q4 disbursements up 15% YoY. Used vehicles and LCV/SCV are being over-indexed; HCV participation is selective.

segments.name: SME (core NBFC)
segments.commentary: Book about INR 8,000 crore, growing 32%, less than 5-6% of portfolio; management targets 30-40% growth from a low base and moved to fully secured lending.

segments.name: Mortgage (MRHFL)
segments.commentary: Subsidiary PAT INR 58 crore vs negative last year; asset quality at 2.4%; subsidiary growth 21%. Board is evaluating whether mortgages sit in the HFC or the standalone NBFC, with formalisation targeted by Q2.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Sri Lanka subsidiary PAT INR 14 crore; insurance broking PAT up 28% YoY; AMC posted its first profit.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term AUM CAGR of 16-18% (FY21-FY31 aspiration of 18-20% decade growth); wheels to grow near market, SME/mortgage/leasing 30-40%.
Management does not give near-term guidance but said sub-teen growth would not be prudent for a lender of its size.
Credit cost to stay within the 1.3-1.7% business-model range; no one-year guidance given.
Full-year NIM of 7.1% seen as reasonable; 7.5% in Q4 not a new normal, with a few bps of upside possible.
Fee-to-assets medium-term 1.4-1.5%, possibly 1.5-1.6% via branch cross-sell; fee income growth to normalise after a near-doubling in FY26.
ROE target of 15% as first stop (versus group 18%); levers are leverage moving toward about 6:1 (currently about 5:1), ROA of 2-2.2%, and OPEX that management says is capped.
PCR overlay could be released in future quarters if headwinds (West Asia conflict, monsoon) do not crystallise.
capex_capacity: Udaan digital stack handled close to 50% of FY26 disbursements; the entire wheels lending stack is 100% live.
Back-office AI (SamurAI) is live in about 20% of business, with sanction-to-disbursement 80% faster.
AI/ML collections drove a 25% improvement in early-bucket collections; 8 multilingual bots handle pre-due and early-bucket calls.
About 1,400 branches being re-orchestrated from fulfilment centres into acquisition and cross-sell centres.
Some AI and digital spend will be capex and some OPEX; no quantification given.
demand_pricing: Management said the H1 FY26 was moderate and momentum rebuilt from Q3, continuing into Q4.
Tractors are the dominant growth vector; base effects will reduce YoY growth rates in FY27.
OEM inventory constraints are making used-vehicle financing more attractive.
CV: recalibrated playbook (used CV added; volatile segments and fleet-operator-heavy segments cut; co-lending with fleet operators in progress).
Collection efficiency in April was in line with plan; Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Assam elections caused temporary disruption, and remittance-dependent states such as Kerala face some stress.
Cross-sell (product per customer) rose to 2.4 from under 2 about 18 months ago; about 24 lakh live customers.

qa_highlights.question: When will AUM growth accelerate from 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects tractor and used-vehicle momentum to continue, with a higher base reducing YoY growth; PV AUM grew 14%; SME and mortgage add diversification, aiming for mid-teens overall with no formal FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7.5% Q4 NIM sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 7.1% is the realistic base, with fee income up 30 bps YoY as a structural lever; 7.5% is not the new normal, and the rights issue benefit on cost of funds will fade as leverage rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for the INR 217 crore overlay?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a macro overlay, not segment-specific, sized on the gross slippage impact of geopolitical and monsoon headwinds, particularly for tractors. It sits within GS3 provisioning and will be revalued quarterly for possible release.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for credit cost and OPEX in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost will stay in the 1.3-1.7% range; management expects revenue growth to outpace OPEX growth, with OPEX to assets range bound at 2.7%.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about ROE beyond 12.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15% ROE first, driven by leverage rising toward about 6:1, ROA of 2-2.2%, and OPEX that is capped; NIM is also a lever.

qa_highlights.question: What borrowings mature in the next year and at what cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 35,000-40,000 crore matures in the next year; the weighted average cost was not disclosed on the call.

risks_watch: INR 217 crore overlay (about 0.3% of AUM-equivalent provisioning) could be released or could crystallise depending on West Asia conflict and monsoon outcomes.
Cost of funds: April capital-market rates spiked after the March peak; management gave no quantified incremental cost. The rights-issue benefit fades as leverage rises.
Tractor portfolio is exposed to monsoon and rural stress; El Nino and fuel or inflation pressures were raised by analysts.
SME scale-up at 30-40% from a low base may carry underwriting risk in a cyclical environment.
Life insurance commissions (about INR 150 crore in FY25) face regulatory risk; FY26 fee income about doubled, partly due to late corporate-agency licensing, and is expected to normalise.
Mortgage business structure (HFC vs NBFC) decision due by Q2 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, asset quality and growth momentum, with a clear prudence stance on the overlay. Management was evasive on specifics not disclosed (weighted average cost of borrowings, life insurance premium, OPEX split, the HFC decision), and declined to give one-year guidance.

I would not want to call 7.5% as a new normal. I would think 7.1% with some few bps here and there improvement as possibilities, but not a 7.1% to 7.5%, for sure.
We do want to get to a 15 very soon.
yes 16% to 18% is the CAGR growth for the medium term.

adds.what: About 1,400 branches being re-orchestrated from fulfilment centres into acquisition and cross-sell centres (re-purposing, not new capacity)

growth.why: Medium-term AUM CAGR guided at 16-18% (FY27-FY31) with SME, mortgage and leasing at 30-40%, backed by tractor momentum, digital stack and cross-sell, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts with numbers were given, and management declined near-term guidance.
